name: Carved disc
idea: A solid disc with two triangular wedges with parallel long edges cut in from opposite sides, so the circle itself becomes an N.

name: Two quarters
idea: Two quarter discs in opposite corners of a square, with the radius set so their arcs touch at exactly one point, the centre.

name: Negative N
idea: Two identical right triangles and nothing else: the N is never drawn, it is the green of the disc left between them.

name: Cut disc
idea: A disc cut along a line 15 degrees off vertical, its two halves slid in opposite directions along the cut so they meet only along that edge.

name: Round counters
idea: A square block whose two counters are quarter circles of one radius, centred on the inner corners of the stems, so the diagonal is drawn only by what they leave.

name: Razor N
idea: A single eight-point polygon: each stem tapers from the full width at its joint to a needle at its free end, and the diagonal keeps a constant weight.

name: Meeting point
idea: The market's down triangle above its up triangle, the same shape sheared in opposite directions, touching only at their tips in the centre.

name: Three lines
idea: Three bars of equal width on a 45-degree grid: two run in from the left and become one at a single joint.

name: Three beams
idea: Three 16-degree wedges with 21-degree gaps, all starting from one corner of a square and ending on its edges, so every line leads to one vertex.

name: Candles
idea: Four equal candlestick bars on one grid: two full height and two shorter, one hung from the top line and one standing on the baseline, so the row reads as an N.
